title: Hugo's Wobbly Tower
markdown:
Hugo wanted to build a tall tower in his toy shop, a cozy nook filled with sunshine. He stacked round balls next to blocky cars, and put a fuzzy bear right on top.

A gentle breeze came in. The tower wobbled and tumbled. The toys rolled and clattered everywhere.

Bloom the bee buzzed in. “Oh dear!” she hummed.

Miss Maple, the wise tree outside, rustled her leaves. “Patience now,” she whispered. “Every tumble teaches.”

Hugo looked at the jumbled toys. How could he build it so it wouldn’t fall?

Bloom zipped around. She nudged a round ball. It rolled away. She nudged a blocky car. It wiggled but stayed put. “Hugo! The round ones roll, and the flat ones stay still!”

Hugo picked up a ball. It felt ready to roll. He pushed it. It slid like a tiny explorer. He picked up a blocky car. It slid too, but stayed more grounded. “You’re right, Bloom. Round toys roll. Flat toys stay steady.”

Miss Maple’s leaves rustled. “Flat sides are like steady feet. Round sides are like cheerful wheels.”

So Hugo built his tower again. This time he placed the round toys inside sturdy boxes, like treasures. He stacked the steady flat toys high, their sides fitting together like puzzle pieces. His new tower was grand and tall, reaching for the sunbeams.

Bloom buzzed a happy tune. The breeze came again, the same small indoor puff. The tower did not tumble. Hugo smiled, a quiet wonder blooming inside him. Round ones roll. Flat ones stay put. The bear sat on a box this time, and that, it turned out, was enough.
